_meta.how_to_use: Apply the statewide_baseline rules everywhere in California, then the record for the place the family rides. A local record never relaxes a state rule. The under-12 power in VC 21214.7 is repealed Jan 1, 2029.
notes_on_inputs: ideas_red_team.md says VC 312.5(a) requires a motor 'under 750 watts'. The current text (SB 1271, effective Jan 1, 2025) says 'does not exceed 750 watts', so exactly 750 W qualifies. 'Less than 750 watts' was the pre-2025 wording, which the Carlsbad and Encinitas pages still repeat.

ideas_red_team.md gives a second reading of Jun 30, 2026 for the City of San Diego (from NBC 7). The City's own Jun 23 release says Jul 7, 2026. The City's Aug 7 release gives the effective date as Aug 13, 2026.

ideas_red_team.md left open whether state law bars Class 3 from Class I bike paths. It does not since AB 1909 (effective Jan 1, 2023). VC 21207.5(b) lets locals ban e-bikes or a class on equestrian, hiking and recreational trails, and VC 21206 lets locals regulate operation on bicycle facilities.

statewide_baseline.quote: A local authority within the County of San Diego, or the County of San Diego in unincorporated areas, may, by ordinance or resolution, prohibit a person under 12 years of age from operating a class 1 or 2 electric bicycle.
statewide_baseline.notes: First 60 days warnings only, then a $25 infraction. No court record if a parent shows a completed e-bike safety program within 120 days. Parent jointly liable. Current text amended by AB 1170 (Stats. 2025, ch. 67), effective Jan 1, 2026.

statewide_baseline.quote: A person under 18 years of age shall not operate a bicycle ... upon a street, bikeway ... or any other public bicycle path or trail unless they are wearing a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet
A person under 16 years of age shall not operate a class 3 electric bicycle.
statewide_baseline.notes: 21213(b) also requires a helmet for every Class 3 operator and passenger.

statewide_baseline.quote: operating a vehicle with fewer than four wheels that does not meet the definition of an electric bicycle ... capable of exclusively propelling the vehicle in excess of 20 miles per hour ... not licensed to operate the vehicle
statewide_baseline.notes: Added by AB 875 (Stats. 2025, ch. 168). Also allows removal of a Class 3 ridden by someone under 16. From Jan 1, 2027, SB 1167 (Stats. 2026, ch. 846, approved Sep 30, 2026) amends two sections. SEC. 42 amends VC 23135, which already exists for modified mopeds, adding a bar on any 2- or 3-wheeled electric device able to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone on highways unless it fits a road-legal class. SEC. 41 amends this section, adding 22651.08(a)(3), removal of an unauthorized device on a highway or public right-of-way.

statewide_baseline.quote: An “electric bicycle” is a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts of power.

local_age_limits.quote: Persons under 12 years of age are prohibited from operating Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles. This prohibition applies to all public rights-of-way, parks, paths, trails, and any other area open to bicycle travel.
local_age_limits.notes: Adopted under VC 21214.7(b), final passage Jul 14, 2026. Infraction with a $25 fine (SDMC 84.20(b)(1)), after warnings only for the first 60 days (SDMC 84.20(a), VC 21214.7(c)(1)(A)). A parent or legal guardian with custody or control of an unemancipated minor is jointly and severally liable (SDMC 84.20(b)(3)). The enacted text gives no calendar date for the first citation. The City release gives Oct 12, 2026. A count under Code Civ. Proc. 12 (excluding Aug 13) makes Oct 12 the 60th warning day, so Oct 13 would be the first citation day under that reading. The app keeps Oct 12, the City's date and the earlier one. The ordinance is repealed Jan 1, 2029 (O-22123 N.S. Sec. 2, and the editor's note to SDMC 84.19) unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended or made permanent, in which case it stays in effect as long as the state law does, so the end date must track the statute. That sunset also covers the SDMC 84.21 helmet and passenger rules.

helmet_rules.citation: SDMC 84.21(a) and (c) (O-22123 N.S.), Cal. Veh. Code 21212, 21213
helmet_rules.quote: All operators and passengers of electric bicycles shall comply with the helmet requirements in the California Vehicle Code, including sections 21212 and 21213. Helmets shall be properly fitted and fastened at all times while operating the electric bicycle. ... Section 84.21 applies to all electric bicycle operators.
helmet_rules.notes: 84.21(a) incorporates state helmet law, under 18 on any e-bike and all ages on Class 3 (VC 21212(a), 21213(b)), and says helmets shall be properly fitted and fastened at all times while operating. 84.21(c) says the section applies to all electric bicycle operators. Recital F says the Council intends to reinforce existing state requirements, so one reading only requires required helmets to be fitted and fastened, but (c) supports a helmet rule for every operator. That question is open, so a City answer always lists a helmet for every rider, at any age (lib/rules/local.ts, sd_helmet_all_riders). Text read in the 8-2026 SDMC Ch. 8 Art. 4 PDF on Oct 19, 2026, matching O-22123 N.S. page 4. The section ends Jan 1, 2029 with the rest of O-22123 unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended. The app keeps the helmet line after that, since wearing one is never wrong.

other_local_rules.quote: Electric bicycle operators are prohibited from carrying a passenger unless the electric bicycle is specifically designed and manufactured to carry more than one person and is equipped with a separate seat or saddle for each passenger
other_local_rules.notes: Stricter than VC 21204(b), which only requires a separate seat attached to the bicycle. An aftermarket seat that is legal under state law is not enough in the City. Repealed Jan 1, 2029 with the rest of O-22123 unless the VC 21214.7 sunset is extended.

other_local_rules.quote: It is unlawful for any person to operate any motorized transportation device in the following locations: (1) on the public walkway on Ocean Front Walk in Mission Beach
other_local_rules.notes: A motorized transportation device includes an electric bicycle, rented or owned (SDMC 83.0302 uses the VC 312.5 meaning). Covers Ocean Front Walk (South Mission Beach Jetty to Law St), Bayside Walk (San Diego Place to Corona Oriente Rd), the east Mission Bay walkway (De Anza Rd to South Shores) and the La Jolla Shores boardwalk (Avenida De La Playa to Kellogg Park). Exceptions for physically disabled persons and City law enforcement.

other_local_rules.quote: No person shall operate a bicycle upon any sidewalk fronting any commercial business establishment unless official signs are posted authorizing such use.
other_local_rules.notes: VC 231 says an electric bicycle is a bicycle, and SDMC 81.0101 adopts Vehicle Code definitions, so 84.09(a) reaches e-bikes. SDMC 84.04 separately bars riding any vehicle on any sidewalk, and VC 670 excludes only devices moved exclusively by human power, so an e-bike may count as a vehicle under 84.04. Whether e-bikes may ride on other sidewalks is unclear, so the app never implies they may. SDMC 84.09 was last amended in 1992.

other_local_rules.quote: Bicycles. It is unlawful to ride a bicycle except: (1) where posted to authorize bicycle riding; or (2) on any designated bikeway; or (3) on any road designated and established for automotive traffic; or (4) on paved and unpaved roads within a park used as fire or service roads by authorized motor vehicles unless otherwise posted. Motorcycles or any other motorized vehicles are prohibited except on roads designated and established for automotive traffic.
other_local_rules.notes: Parks by definition include open space, beaches and perimeter sidewalks (SDMC 63.0102(b)). Treat e-bikes on park paths that are not posted or designated bikeways as not allowed. Whether an e-bike is a motorized vehicle under this section is unclear. SDMC 63.0109 sets an 8 mph limit for all wheeled transport on Ocean Front Walk and listed Mission Bay paths. Read in the 9-2024 edition.

local_age_limits.citation: Encinitas Council Agenda Report, Aug 19, 2026, Item 12C
local_age_limits.quote: Amending the EMC to require e-bike riders to be 12 years old would make Encinitas consistent with those cities.
local_age_limits.notes: No age provision in EMC Ch. 14.56 (https://ecode360.com/44479706) or anywhere else in the code read on Oct 19, 2026.
